facts: Monster pathing is home-tethered, so path cost does not grow with map size. Wander picks GetRandomReachablePointInRadius(Home, max(HomeRange,200)) (Source/CL9/Monsters/CL9Monster.cpp:1130-1132). Chase gives up once the monster is more than HomeRange from home (CL9Monster.cpp:1240-1241). Return paths to HomeLocation (CL9Monster.cpp:1063-1064). Search hops use a 300 cm radius (CL9Monster.cpp:52, 628). HomeRange is 840 for chicken and pig, 1200 for raccoon and 2280 for goose (docs/plan/data/monster/chicken.md:61, raccoon.md:37, goose.md:16, pig.md:50).

Pathing is a synchronous FindPathToLocationSynchronously call after projecting both ends with a 500x500x500 extent (CL9Monster.cpp:55, 1154-1170). Chase and stalk re-path every 0.5 s (CL9Monster.cpp:49, 688-693, 892-900).

Every monster ticks every frame and has no tick interval or significance LOD (CL9Monster.cpp:71, 174-192). On the host the tick runs HostTickAI plus TickFootstep. TickHitFlash, TickHitFeel and TickStateSounds run on every machine.

SenseTick loops over characters only (four or fewer). It traces line of sight only when the character is within SightRange, so far monsters cost no traces (CL9Monster.cpp:960-971, 1012-1016). The asleep wake check loops over characters only (CL9Monster.cpp:501-514).

Moving monsters do a swept AddActorWorldOffset plus SetActorRotation every tick (CL9Monster.cpp:1195-1198). The root sphere overlaps all channels except WorldStatic (blocked) and Camera (ignored) (CL9Monster.cpp:77-83). WaypointTolerance is 25 cm (CL9Monster.cpp:39).

The O(N) monster loops (kill alarm, pack alarm, execute anchor) run per event, not per tick (CL9Monster.cpp:1541-1573, 1640-1651, 1868-1879). TryBeginExecute is gated by ExecuteRadius before the sweep (CL9Monster.cpp:1905-1911).

The monster mesh keeps the engine default VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption = AlwaysTickPoseAndRefreshBones (UE_5.8 Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Private/Components/SkeletalMeshComponent.cpp:446). Only the player overrides it (Source/CL9/Character/CL9Character.cpp:147). So the host animates every monster, seen or not.

Measured costs: monster skeletal animation is the largest single game-thread item at about 0.23 ms per monster (docs/systems/performance.md:118-119). Chase with 5, 10 and 20 monsters measured 10.5, 11.3 and 12.8 ms, about 0.15 ms per monster. Spawning 10 monsters at once took 98 ms (performance.md:177). Budgets are 16.7 ms per frame and 4 ms or less of CL9 game-thread code with 4 players and the maximum monster spawn (performance.md:16-18).

Monsters replicate movement at 20 Hz (Source/CL9/Core/CL9ActorBase.cpp:8-9, CL9Monster.cpp:72). They keep the engine NetCullDistanceSquared of 225000000, which is 150 m (UE_5.8 Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Private/Actor.cpp:312). Clients run no AI (CL9Monster.cpp:184-192). On re-entering relevancy, a client runs LoadData again (SetSkeletalMesh and SetAnimInstanceClass, CL9Monster.cpp:120-167).
All monsters spawn synchronously in StartNight right after the clock starts (Source/CL9/GameMode/CL9GameMode.cpp:214-223, 544-565). Nothing spawns later in the night.

The site map, and so the dynamic navmesh build, is made in the lobby, not at night: at StartPlay (CL9GameMode.cpp:768-773) and on every return to the lobby (CL9GameMode.cpp:270-271). The night falls back to building one only if there is no seed (CL9GameMode.cpp:206-212). Nothing gates night start on navigation finishing.

Project navigation config sets only RuntimeGeneration=Dynamic (Config/DefaultEngine.ini:85-86). Engine defaults are TileSizeUU=1000 and CellSize=19 (UE_5.8 Engine/Config/BaseEngine.ini:3052-3053), with invokers off (bGenerateNavigationOnlyAroundNavigationInvokers=false at NavigationSystem.cpp:936). Clients create a navigation system only when bAllowClientSideNavigation is set (NavigationSystem.cpp:6541), and the project does not set it.

Farm navigation today: NavBounds is stretched to 465 x 440 m, which is about 2,070 tiles at 10 m. The runtime build finishes within about 20 s (docs/systems/map.md:191-195). The QA nav_map in Saved/QA/stage_pie_Lvl_Farm.json is 41x42 cells at 10 m and all '#', so empty ground inside the bounds is navmeshed too. setup_stage.py sizes one box per level and deletes the saved RecastNavMesh (Tools/Unreal/setup_stage.py:159-196).

Recast tile capacity is summed over every inclusion bounds box, so several NavMeshBoundsVolumes are supported (UE_5.8 RecastNavMeshGenerator.cpp:5133-5163, 5748-5773). The hard-limit error says to use bigger tiles or raise TileNumberHardLimit (RecastNavMeshGenerator.cpp:5768-5772).

ISM navigation export scans every instance of the component on each per-tile query (UE_5.8 Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Public/InstancedStaticMeshComponentHelper.h:148-167). CL9SiteMap builds one ISM per (seg kind, mesh) and one per (prop mesh, solid) across the whole site, all nav-relevant (Source/CL9/World/CL9SiteMap.cpp:405-425, 656-683). Instances are added before RegisterComponent (CL9SiteMap.cpp:504-581), so registration happens once per component.

Movable nav-relevant things dirty the dynamic navmesh at runtime: promoted carts block Pawn (Source/CL9/Items/CL9Item.cpp:558-565, and PrimitiveComponent.cpp:3684-3686 makes Pawn-blocking components nav-relevant), and the CL9FlapIn body affects navigation (Source/CL9/World/CL9FlapIn.cpp:25).

ACL9SiteMap::Find returns the first site map (CL9SiteMap.cpp:165-176). The night spawner reads points and depth bands from that single layout (CL9GameMode.cpp:504-515, 600-613). The generator span cap is clamp(ceil(sqrt(N*6))*2, 16, 128) (Source/CL9/World/CL9SiteLayout.cpp:866).

The farm QA records only +20, +50 and +90 s samples after cl9.night (Tools/Unreal/qa_farm_stage_pie.py:96-122). The last run had 22 monsters, all on the navmesh, but only 8 ever moved more than 150 cm by +90 s, with a frame average of 11.4 ms (Saved/QA/stage_pie_Lvl_Farm.json). So today's 'all active' baseline is mostly idle or asleep monsters.

Lethal Company code defaults for power caps are indoor 8, outdoor 15 and daytime 20 (docs/reference/lethal/lethal-monsters.md:403-407). Measured moon values (docs/reference/lethal/lethal-map.md:192-207): Titan size 2.2 with indoor 18, outdoor 7, daytime 20. Artifice is 1.8 with 13/13/15. Liquidation is 1.6 with 13/13/20. March is 1.75 with 14/12/14. Rend and Dine are 1.8 with 10 indoor. Experimentation is 1.0 with 4/8/5. Embrion's outdoor 70 is an outlier.

Lethal per-enemy power and caps (lethal-monsters.md:595-629): indoor enemies cost 1-3 power, for example Hoarding bug, Nutcracker and Masked at 1 with max 10, and Flowerman, Crawler and Jester at 3. Outdoor: MouthDog 2 (max 8), ForestGiant 3 (max 3), Baboon hawk 0.5 (max 15).

Lethal spawns ramp over the day. Nothing spawns until currentDayTime > 85 of totalTime 700. Batches come every 2 in-game hours, each clamped to at most 20 and to free vents. Kills refund power (lethal-monsters.md:449-462, 543-563, 387-389). Every enemy 'thinks' on AIIntervalTime 0.2 s, about 5 Hz, with no distance sleep (lethal-monsters.md:53-63).

CL9 farm counts: the zone base sums are 34-45 monsters (Tools/Unreal/stages/farm.json:26-28). MonsterCountCurve runs 0.6 on day 1, 1.0 on day 5 and 1.5 on day 10 (docs/plan/data/progression.md:29). That gives 20-27 on day 1 (25 observed, map.md:194) and 51-68 on day 10.

objections.target: Nav: 'dynamic navmesh over all districts + yard' (one whole-bounds box as today)
objections.problem: A single box around ~1.1 km at 5x is about 12-13k tiles at the default 10 m tile, and about 25k at 10x. Even if build time is linear from the farm's ~2,070 tiles in under 20 s, that is about 2 min at 5x and about 4 min at 10x. The build runs in the lobby, which has no minimum length, and nothing stops the night from starting before navigation is done. Monsters standing on unbuilt tiles then keep failing projection and stay put, retrying StartNewWander every 0.5 s. Yards and gaps between districts get navmesh that no monster can use, because every monster is tethered to its home.
objections.alternative: Give the stage fixed district slots: each district's position and footprint is set in the stage JSON and the seed only fills its contents. setup_stage.py then places one NavMeshBoundsVolume per slot, sized to that slot's day-10 span plus a HomeRange margin of about 25 m. Leave yards without navmesh until a yard monster exists. Tile capacity sums per volume, so several volumes are supported. Add a host gate so the truck cannot leave for the night while UNavigationSystemV1 reports a build in progress, or measure and enforce a minimum lobby time.

objections.target: Nav: navigation invokers on monsters to satisfy 'always active'
objections.problem: It satisfies the rule only on paper. Invokers register when monsters spawn, and monsters spawn at StartNight, so the navmesh build moves from the hidden lobby into the first seconds or minutes of the night, and every monster is frozen until its tiles exist. The invoker flag is NavigationSystem-wide (default false), so it changes henhouse, farm and pigfarm too. Spawn points cover the whole layout, so invoker discs around ~50-100 home-tethered monsters cover almost all of each district anyway. The only gain is leaving yards without navmesh, which per-district bounds already give, deterministically and in the lobby.
objections.alternative: Do not use invokers. Use per-district bounds volumes as above. If invokers are ever wanted, put them on fixed per-district anchor actors that exist from the lobby, not on monsters.
objections.evidence: NavigationSystem.cpp:936, 5437; CL9GameMode.cpp:214-223; CL9GameMode.cpp:519-541 (spawn points span the layout)

objections.target: Rendering/nav: 'existing ISM-per-segment approach' carried to districts
objections.problem: Recast's per-tile export of an ISM component scans every instance of that component on each tile query. CL9SiteMap makes one ISM per (kind, mesh) for the whole site. If districts are built as one SiteMap actor, or share the ComponentFor maps, gathering costs tiles x instances. That is about 13k x 17k, roughly 221M bounds tests at 5x, against about 7M on the farm (30x worse), and about 120x worse at 10x. It is quadratic, not linear.
objections.alternative: Make the design say it explicitly: each district is its own ACL9SiteMap actor with its own ISM component set, or ISMs are chunked per sector of about 100 m. Each tile then scans only that district's instances and the cost stays at the farm's level times K. Note that ACL9SiteMap::Find and the night spawner assume a single map and must loop over all of them.

objections.target: Nav: 'larger tiles' as the tile-count fix
objections.problem: A 20 m tile cuts the tile count by 4x, but voxelisation work per tile grows about 4x, so total rasterisation stays roughly the same. The real gain is per-tile overhead and the ISM scan count, which per-district components already fix. The cost is that every runtime dirty area, such as a cart moving or a flap opening, rebuilds a 400 m² tile instead of a 100 m² one.
objections.alternative: Keep TileSizeUU 1000 as the default. Measure 1000 against 2000 at 5x only after per-district ISM components and per-district bounds are in place, and pick a size from the measured build time and cart-push rebuild cost.

objections.target: Draft says nothing about the always-on per-monster cost on the host
objections.problem: The host animates every monster whether it is visible or not, because the engine default AlwaysTickPoseAndRefreshBones is never overridden for monsters. At about 0.15-0.23 ms per monster, 80 monsters cost about 12-18 ms and 100 monsters about 15-23 ms of game thread. That blows both the 16.7 ms frame target and the 4 ms CL9 budget before AI is counted. Today's farm number (11.4 ms with 22 monsters) hides this because only 8 of the 22 ever moved.
objections.alternative: Split 'active' into behaviour and presentation. AI, movement and senses always run, per the user's decision. The monster MeshComponent uses OnlyTickMontagesWhenNotRendered, or OnlyTickPoseWhenRendered, plus update-rate optimisation. Hits use the root sphere and the execute camera only matters when someone is close, so gameplay does not depend on unseen bones. Optionally, also lower the think rate when no player is within about 50 m, matching Lethal's 0.2 s AIIntervalTime, which applies to all of its enemies. If so, clamp the movement step so it does not overshoot the 25 cm WaypointTolerance.

objections.target: Population spawn timing (unchanged StartNight bulk spawn)
objections.problem: Every monster spawns in one frame in StartNight. The measured cost was 98 ms for 10 monsters at once, so 45-80 monsters means roughly a 0.45-0.8 s host hitch at the moment the night starts.
objections.alternative: Spread spawning over frames, for example a few per frame per district during the first 1-2 s. Or adopt a Lethal-style ramp in which far districts fill in batches over the night. A ramp does not conflict with 'never sleep or despawn by distance'.

objections.target: Population count ('sensible by comparison with Lethal')
objections.problem: Scaling the farm by 5x gives 100-135 monsters on day 1 and 255-340 on day 10, which is not workable on the host. The farm on day 10 (51-68) is already 2-3x Lethal's largest-moon peak for a single facility. Titan allows 18 indoor plus 7 outdoor power, which is about 9-15 indoor and 2-14 outdoor enemies at 1-3 power each, about 12-25 concurrent, reached only late in the day.
objections.alternative: Treat each district (about 200 modules, about a 1-minute spine like one Lethal facility) as one Lethal-moon equivalent and give it a power budget. Suggested CL9 powers: chicken and sheep 1, goose and raccoon 2, pig 3. Per district, day 1 runs from 6 power (near) to 12 power (far), which spans Lethal's Experimentation 4 to Rend 10. Day 10 runs from 12 to 18, which is Titan. At 5x that is about 45 monsters on day 1 (near 5, two mid at 8, two far at 12), about 65 on day 5, and a hard cap of about 80 on day 10. Count is capped by power the way Lethal does it, and the day curve shifts the species mix once the cap is reached. 10x keeps the same per-district budget, about 90 on day 1 and 160 on day 10, and only proceeds if 5x holds its frame budget with 80 monsters all awake.

objections.target: QA plan: 'qa_farm_stage_pie.py and layout tests at the new size'
objections.problem: The script starts timing at cl9.night and samples only at +20, +50 and +90 s. It never measures how long navigation takes after SetSiteMap, or the worst case where the night starts at once. The 500-unit projection extent passes a monster whose own tile is missing as long as a neighbouring tile exists. It also does not force monsters awake, so the 'always active' cost goes untested.
objections.alternative: Add these to the giant QA. Record seconds from SetSiteMap until IsNavigationBeingBuilt is false, along with tile count and navmesh memory. Run a night started immediately after the lobby build. Project with a small extent, about 100 units. Run a pass with every monster forced awake and wandering through a cheat, and record host game-thread ms with stat dumpframe. Add a scripted walk across yards to see client relevancy churn.

objections.target: Replication at district scale (not addressed in the draft)
objections.problem: With the 150 m default cull distance and 390 m districts, players crossing yards make monster actor channels open and close repeatedly on clients. Each re-entry runs LoadData, which sets the skeletal mesh and the ABP. This keeps client CPU bounded, which is good, but the churn cost and any hitch have not been measured.
objections.alternative: Keep the default cull distance and do not make monsters always relevant. Measure re-entry hitches in the yard-walk QA. Only if hitches show up, pool the anim instance or tune NetCullDistance per species.

The real wall-clock cost of the ISM per-tile instance scan at farm and 5x sizes. The code path is confirmed in InstancedStaticMeshComponentHelper.h:148-167 and the magnitude is my estimate.
Recast navmesh memory per tile and in total at 5x and 10x. Measure with stat navigation or LogMemUsed.
Host per-monster cost once animation is culled. I estimate tens of microseconds (sweep, overlap update, tick overhead). Measure with every monster forced awake and wandering.
Whether the monster Blueprint subclasses or ABPs already override VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption, or rely on anim notifies for gameplay. I checked C++ only.
The default of bAllowClientSideNavigation. It is not set in project config, so I assume the engine default of false and that only the host builds navmesh.
Client relevancy-churn hitch when crossing yards (actor channel re-open plus LoadData).
Whether the 98 ms per 10 simultaneous spawns scales linearly to 45-80.

The proposed CL9 power values per species (chicken 1 … pig 3). These are my mapping by danger and need balance sign-off.

facts: Monster pathing is home-tethered, so path cost does not grow with map size. Wander picks GetRandomReachablePointInRadius(Home, max(HomeRange,200)) (Source/CL9/Monsters/CL9Monster.cpp:1130-1132). Chase gives up once the monster is more than HomeRange from home (CL9Monster.cpp:1240-1241). Return paths to HomeLocation (CL9Monster.cpp:1063-1064). Search hops use a 300 cm radius (CL9Monster.cpp:52, 628). HomeRange is 840 for chicken and pig, 1200 for raccoon and 2280 for goose (docs/plan/data/monster/chicken.md:61, raccoon.md:37, goose.md:16, pig.md:50).

Pathing is a synchronous FindPathToLocationSynchronously call after projecting both ends with a 500x500x500 extent (CL9Monster.cpp:55, 1154-1170). Chase and stalk re-path every 0.5 s (CL9Monster.cpp:49, 688-693, 892-900).

Every monster ticks every frame and has no tick interval or significance LOD (CL9Monster.cpp:71, 174-192). On the host the tick runs HostTickAI plus TickFootstep. TickHitFlash, TickHitFeel and TickStateSounds run on every machine.

SenseTick loops over characters only (four or fewer). It traces line of sight only when the character is within SightRange, so far monsters cost no traces (CL9Monster.cpp:960-971, 1012-1016). The asleep wake check loops over characters only (CL9Monster.cpp:501-514).

Moving monsters do a swept AddActorWorldOffset plus SetActorRotation every tick (CL9Monster.cpp:1195-1198). The root sphere overlaps all channels except WorldStatic (blocked) and Camera (ignored) (CL9Monster.cpp:77-83). WaypointTolerance is 25 cm (CL9Monster.cpp:39).

The O(N) monster loops (kill alarm, pack alarm, execute anchor) run per event, not per tick (CL9Monster.cpp:1541-1573, 1640-1651, 1868-1879). TryBeginExecute is gated by ExecuteRadius before the sweep (CL9Monster.cpp:1905-1911).

The monster mesh keeps the engine default VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption = AlwaysTickPoseAndRefreshBones (UE_5.8 Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Private/Components/SkeletalMeshComponent.cpp:446). Only the player overrides it (Source/CL9/Character/CL9Character.cpp:147). So the host animates every monster, seen or not.

Measured costs: monster skeletal animation is the largest single game-thread item at about 0.23 ms per monster (docs/systems/performance.md:118-119). Chase with 5, 10 and 20 monsters measured 10.5, 11.3 and 12.8 ms, about 0.15 ms per monster. Spawning 10 monsters at once took 98 ms (performance.md:177). Budgets are 16.7 ms per frame and 4 ms or less of CL9 game-thread code with 4 players and the maximum monster spawn (performance.md:16-18).

Monsters replicate movement at 20 Hz (Source/CL9/Core/CL9ActorBase.cpp:8-9, CL9Monster.cpp:72). They keep the engine NetCullDistanceSquared of 225000000, which is 150 m (UE_5.8 Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Private/Actor.cpp:312). Clients run no AI (CL9Monster.cpp:184-192). On re-entering relevancy, a client runs LoadData again (SetSkeletalMesh and SetAnimInstanceClass, CL9Monster.cpp:120-167).
All monsters spawn synchronously in StartNight right after the clock starts (Source/CL9/GameMode/CL9GameMode.cpp:214-223, 544-565). Nothing spawns later in the night.

The site map, and so the dynamic navmesh build, is made in the lobby, not at night: at StartPlay (CL9GameMode.cpp:768-773) and on every return to the lobby (CL9GameMode.cpp:270-271). The night falls back to building one only if there is no seed (CL9GameMode.cpp:206-212). Nothing gates night start on navigation finishing.

Project navigation config sets only RuntimeGeneration=Dynamic (Config/DefaultEngine.ini:85-86). Engine defaults are TileSizeUU=1000 and CellSize=19 (UE_5.8 Engine/Config/BaseEngine.ini:3052-3053), with invokers off (bGenerateNavigationOnlyAroundNavigationInvokers=false at NavigationSystem.cpp:936). Clients create a navigation system only when bAllowClientSideNavigation is set (NavigationSystem.cpp:6541), and the project does not set it.

Farm navigation today: NavBounds is stretched to 465 x 440 m, which is about 2,070 tiles at 10 m. The runtime build finishes within about 20 s (docs/systems/map.md:191-195). The QA nav_map in Saved/QA/stage_pie_Lvl_Farm.json is 41x42 cells at 10 m and all '#', so empty ground inside the bounds is navmeshed too. setup_stage.py sizes one box per level and deletes the saved RecastNavMesh (Tools/Unreal/setup_stage.py:159-196).

Recast tile capacity is summed over every inclusion bounds box, so several NavMeshBoundsVolumes are supported (UE_5.8 RecastNavMeshGenerator.cpp:5133-5163, 5748-5773). The hard-limit error says to use bigger tiles or raise TileNumberHardLimit (RecastNavMeshGenerator.cpp:5768-5772).

ISM navigation export scans every instance of the component on each per-tile query (UE_5.8 Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Public/InstancedStaticMeshComponentHelper.h:148-167). CL9SiteMap builds one ISM per (seg kind, mesh) and one per (prop mesh, solid) across the whole site, all nav-relevant (Source/CL9/World/CL9SiteMap.cpp:405-425, 656-683). Instances are added before RegisterComponent (CL9SiteMap.cpp:504-581), so registration happens once per component.

Movable nav-relevant things dirty the dynamic navmesh at runtime: promoted carts block Pawn (Source/CL9/Items/CL9Item.cpp:558-565, and PrimitiveComponent.cpp:3684-3686 makes Pawn-blocking components nav-relevant), and the CL9FlapIn body affects navigation (Source/CL9/World/CL9FlapIn.cpp:25).

ACL9SiteMap::Find returns the first site map (CL9SiteMap.cpp:165-176). The night spawner reads points and depth bands from that single layout (CL9GameMode.cpp:504-515, 600-613). The generator span cap is clamp(ceil(sqrt(N*6))*2, 16, 128) (Source/CL9/World/CL9SiteLayout.cpp:866).

The farm QA records only +20, +50 and +90 s samples after cl9.night (Tools/Unreal/qa_farm_stage_pie.py:96-122). The last run had 22 monsters, all on the navmesh, but only 8 ever moved more than 150 cm by +90 s, with a frame average of 11.4 ms (Saved/QA/stage_pie_Lvl_Farm.json). So today's 'all active' baseline is mostly idle or asleep monsters.

Lethal Company code defaults for power caps are indoor 8, outdoor 15 and daytime 20 (docs/reference/lethal/lethal-monsters.md:403-407). Measured moon values (docs/reference/lethal/lethal-map.md:192-207): Titan size 2.2 with indoor 18, outdoor 7, daytime 20. Artifice is 1.8 with 13/13/15. Liquidation is 1.6 with 13/13/20. March is 1.75 with 14/12/14. Rend and Dine are 1.8 with 10 indoor. Experimentation is 1.0 with 4/8/5. Embrion's outdoor 70 is an outlier.

Lethal per-enemy power and caps (lethal-monsters.md:595-629): indoor enemies cost 1-3 power, for example Hoarding bug, Nutcracker and Masked at 1 with max 10, and Flowerman, Crawler and Jester at 3. Outdoor: MouthDog 2 (max 8), ForestGiant 3 (max 3), Baboon hawk 0.5 (max 15).

facts: Monster pathing is home-tethered, so path cost does not grow with map size. Wander picks GetRandomReachablePointInRadius(Home, max(HomeRange,200)) (Source/CL9/Monsters/CL9Monster.cpp:1130-1132). Chase gives up once the monster is more than HomeRange from home (CL9Monster.cpp:1240-1241). Return paths to HomeLocation (CL9Monster.cpp:1063-1064). Search hops use a 300 cm radius (CL9Monster.cpp:52, 628). HomeRange is 840 for chicken and pig, 1200 for raccoon and 2280 for goose (docs/plan/data/monster/chicken.md:61, raccoon.md:37, goose.md:16, pig.md:50).

Pathing is a synchronous FindPathToLocationSynchronously call after projecting both ends with a 500x500x500 extent (CL9Monster.cpp:55, 1154-1170). Chase and stalk re-path every 0.5 s (CL9Monster.cpp:49, 688-693, 892-900).

Every monster ticks every frame and has no tick interval or significance LOD (CL9Monster.cpp:71, 174-192). On the host the tick runs HostTickAI plus TickFootstep. TickHitFlash, TickHitFeel and TickStateSounds run on every machine.

SenseTick loops over characters only (four or fewer). It traces line of sight only when the character is within SightRange, so far monsters cost no traces (CL9Monster.cpp:960-971, 1012-1016). The asleep wake check loops over characters only (CL9Monster.cpp:501-514).

Moving monsters do a swept AddActorWorldOffset plus SetActorRotation every tick (CL9Monster.cpp:1195-1198). The root sphere overlaps all channels except WorldStatic (blocked) and Camera (ignored) (CL9Monster.cpp:77-83). WaypointTolerance is 25 cm (CL9Monster.cpp:39).

The O(N) monster loops (kill alarm, pack alarm, execute anchor) run per event, not per tick (CL9Monster.cpp:1541-1573, 1640-1651, 1868-1879). TryBeginExecute is gated by ExecuteRadius before the sweep (CL9Monster.cpp:1905-1911).

The monster mesh keeps the engine default VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption = AlwaysTickPoseAndRefreshBones (UE_5.8 Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Private/Components/SkeletalMeshComponent.cpp:446). Only the player overrides it (Source/CL9/Character/CL9Character.cpp:147). So the host animates every monster, seen or not.

Measured costs: monster skeletal animation is the largest single game-thread item at about 0.23 ms per monster (docs/systems/performance.md:118-119). Chase with 5, 10 and 20 monsters measured 10.5, 11.3 and 12.8 ms, about 0.15 ms per monster. Spawning 10 monsters at once took 98 ms (performance.md:177). Budgets are 16.7 ms per frame and 4 ms or less of CL9 game-thread code with 4 players and the maximum monster spawn (performance.md:16-18).

Monsters replicate movement at 20 Hz (Source/CL9/Core/CL9ActorBase.cpp:8-9, CL9Monster.cpp:72). They keep the engine NetCullDistanceSquared of 225000000, which is 150 m (UE_5.8 Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Private/Actor.cpp:312). Clients run no AI (CL9Monster.cpp:184-192). On re-entering relevancy, a client runs LoadData again (SetSkeletalMesh and SetAnimInstanceClass, CL9Monster.cpp:120-167).
All monsters spawn synchronously in StartNight right after the clock starts (Source/CL9/GameMode/CL9GameMode.cpp:214-223, 544-565). Nothing spawns later in the night.

The site map, and so the dynamic navmesh build, is made in the lobby, not at night: at StartPlay (CL9GameMode.cpp:768-773) and on every return to the lobby (CL9GameMode.cpp:270-271). The night falls back to building one only if there is no seed (CL9GameMode.cpp:206-212). Nothing gates night start on navigation finishing.

Project navigation config sets only RuntimeGeneration=Dynamic (Config/DefaultEngine.ini:85-86). Engine defaults are TileSizeUU=1000 and CellSize=19 (UE_5.8 Engine/Config/BaseEngine.ini:3052-3053), with invokers off (bGenerateNavigationOnlyAroundNavigationInvokers=false at NavigationSystem.cpp:936). Clients create a navigation system only when bAllowClientSideNavigation is set (NavigationSystem.cpp:6541), and the project does not set it.

Farm navigation today: NavBounds is stretched to 465 x 440 m, which is about 2,070 tiles at 10 m. The runtime build finishes within about 20 s (docs/systems/map.md:191-195). The QA nav_map in Saved/QA/stage_pie_Lvl_Farm.json is 41x42 cells at 10 m and all '#', so empty ground inside the bounds is navmeshed too. setup_stage.py sizes one box per level and deletes the saved RecastNavMesh (Tools/Unreal/setup_stage.py:159-196).

Recast tile capacity is summed over every inclusion bounds box, so several NavMeshBoundsVolumes are supported (UE_5.8 RecastNavMeshGenerator.cpp:5133-5163, 5748-5773). The hard-limit error says to use bigger tiles or raise TileNumberHardLimit (RecastNavMeshGenerator.cpp:5768-5772).

ISM navigation export scans every instance of the component on each per-tile query (UE_5.8 Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Public/InstancedStaticMeshComponentHelper.h:148-167). CL9SiteMap builds one ISM per (seg kind, mesh) and one per (prop mesh, solid) across the whole site, all nav-relevant (Source/CL9/World/CL9SiteMap.cpp:405-425, 656-683). Instances are added before RegisterComponent (CL9SiteMap.cpp:504-581), so registration happens once per component.

Movable nav-relevant things dirty the dynamic navmesh at runtime: promoted carts block Pawn (Source/CL9/Items/CL9Item.cpp:558-565, and PrimitiveComponent.cpp:3684-3686 makes Pawn-blocking components nav-relevant), and the CL9FlapIn body affects navigation (Source/CL9/World/CL9FlapIn.cpp:25).

ACL9SiteMap::Find returns the first site map (CL9SiteMap.cpp:165-176). The night spawner reads points and depth bands from that single layout (CL9GameMode.cpp:504-515, 600-613). The generator span cap is clamp(ceil(sqrt(N*6))*2, 16, 128) (Source/CL9/World/CL9SiteLayout.cpp:866).

The farm QA records only +20, +50 and +90 s samples after cl9.night (Tools/Unreal/qa_farm_stage_pie.py:96-122). The last run had 22 monsters, all on the navmesh, but only 8 ever moved more than 150 cm by +90 s, with a frame average of 11.4 ms (Saved/QA/stage_pie_Lvl_Farm.json). So today's 'all active' baseline is mostly idle or asleep monsters.

Lethal Company code defaults for power caps are indoor 8, outdoor 15 and daytime 20 (docs/reference/lethal/lethal-monsters.md:403-407). Measured moon values (docs/reference/lethal/lethal-map.md:192-207): Titan size 2.2 with indoor 18, outdoor 7, daytime 20. Artifice is 1.8 with 13/13/15. Liquidation is 1.6 with 13/13/20. March is 1.75 with 14/12/14. Rend and Dine are 1.8 with 10 indoor. Experimentation is 1.0 with 4/8/5. Embrion's outdoor 70 is an outlier.

Lethal per-enemy power and caps (lethal-monsters.md:595-629): indoor enemies cost 1-3 power, for example Hoarding bug, Nutcracker and Masked at 1 with max 10, and Flowerman, Crawler and Jester at 3. Outdoor: MouthDog 2 (max 8), ForestGiant 3 (max 3), Baboon hawk 0.5 (max 15).

Lethal spawns ramp over the day. Nothing spawns until currentDayTime > 85 of totalTime 700. Batches come every 2 in-game hours, each clamped to at most 20 and to free vents. Kills refund power (lethal-monsters.md:449-462, 543-563, 387-389). Every enemy 'thinks' on AIIntervalTime 0.2 s, about 5 Hz, with no distance sleep (lethal-monsters.md:53-63).

CL9 farm counts: the zone base sums are 34-45 monsters (Tools/Unreal/stages/farm.json:26-28). MonsterCountCurve runs 0.6 on day 1, 1.0 on day 5 and 1.5 on day 10 (docs/plan/data/progression.md:29). That gives 20-27 on day 1 (25 observed, map.md:194) and 51-68 on day 10.

objections.target: Nav: 'dynamic navmesh over all districts + yard' (one whole-bounds box as today)
objections.problem: A single box around ~1.1 km at 5x is about 12-13k tiles at the default 10 m tile, and about 25k at 10x. Even if build time is linear from the farm's ~2,070 tiles in under 20 s, that is about 2 min at 5x and about 4 min at 10x. The build runs in the lobby, which has no minimum length, and nothing stops the night from starting before navigation is done. Monsters standing on unbuilt tiles then keep failing projection and stay put, retrying StartNewWander every 0.5 s. Yards and gaps between districts get navmesh that no monster can use, because every monster is tethered to its home.
objections.alternative: Give the stage fixed district slots: each district's position and footprint is set in the stage JSON and the seed only fills its contents. setup_stage.py then places one NavMeshBoundsVolume per slot, sized to that slot's day-10 span plus a HomeRange margin of about 25 m. Leave yards without navmesh until a yard monster exists. Tile capacity sums per volume, so several volumes are supported. Add a host gate so the truck cannot leave for the night while UNavigationSystemV1 reports a build in progress, or measure and enforce a minimum lobby time.

objections.target: Nav: navigation invokers on monsters to satisfy 'always active'
objections.problem: It satisfies the rule only on paper. Invokers register when monsters spawn, and monsters spawn at StartNight, so the navmesh build moves from the hidden lobby into the first seconds or minutes of the night, and every monster is frozen until its tiles exist. The invoker flag is NavigationSystem-wide (default false), so it changes henhouse, farm and pigfarm too. Spawn points cover the whole layout, so invoker discs around ~50-100 home-tethered monsters cover almost all of each district anyway. The only gain is leaving yards without navmesh, which per-district bounds already give, deterministically and in the lobby.
objections.alternative: Do not use invokers. Use per-district bounds volumes as above. If invokers are ever wanted, put them on fixed per-district anchor actors that exist from the lobby, not on monsters.
objections.evidence: NavigationSystem.cpp:936, 5437; CL9GameMode.cpp:214-223; CL9GameMode.cpp:519-541 (spawn points span the layout)

objections.target: Rendering/nav: 'existing ISM-per-segment approach' carried to districts
objections.problem: Recast's per-tile export of an ISM component scans every instance of that component on each tile query. CL9SiteMap makes one ISM per (kind, mesh) for the whole site. If districts are built as one SiteMap actor, or share the ComponentFor maps, gathering costs tiles x instances. That is about 13k x 17k, roughly 221M bounds tests at 5x, against about 7M on the farm (30x worse), and about 120x worse at 10x. It is quadratic, not linear.
objections.alternative: Make the design say it explicitly: each district is its own ACL9SiteMap actor with its own ISM component set, or ISMs are chunked per sector of about 100 m. Each tile then scans only that district's instances and the cost stays at the farm's level times K. Note that ACL9SiteMap::Find and the night spawner assume a single map and must loop over all of them.

objections.target: Nav: 'larger tiles' as the tile-count fix
objections.problem: A 20 m tile cuts the tile count by 4x, but voxelisation work per tile grows about 4x, so total rasterisation stays roughly the same. The real gain is per-tile overhead and the ISM scan count, which per-district components already fix. The cost is that every runtime dirty area, such as a cart moving or a flap opening, rebuilds a 400 m² tile instead of a 100 m² one.
objections.alternative: Keep TileSizeUU 1000 as the default. Measure 1000 against 2000 at 5x only after per-district ISM components and per-district bounds are in place, and pick a size from the measured build time and cart-push rebuild cost.

objections.target: Draft says nothing about the always-on per-monster cost on the host
objections.problem: The host animates every monster whether it is visible or not, because the engine default AlwaysTickPoseAndRefreshBones is never overridden for monsters. At about 0.15-0.23 ms per monster, 80 monsters cost about 12-18 ms and 100 monsters about 15-23 ms of game thread. That blows both the 16.7 ms frame target and the 4 ms CL9 budget before AI is counted. Today's farm number (11.4 ms with 22 monsters) hides this because only 8 of the 22 ever moved.
objections.alternative: Split 'active' into behaviour and presentation. AI, movement and senses always run, per the user's decision. The monster MeshComponent uses OnlyTickMontagesWhenNotRendered, or OnlyTickPoseWhenRendered, plus update-rate optimisation. Hits use the root sphere and the execute camera only matters when someone is close, so gameplay does not depend on unseen bones. Optionally, also lower the think rate when no player is within about 50 m, matching Lethal's 0.2 s AIIntervalTime, which applies to all of its enemies. If so, clamp the movement step so it does not overshoot the 25 cm WaypointTolerance.

objections.target: Population spawn timing (unchanged StartNight bulk spawn)
objections.problem: Every monster spawns in one frame in StartNight. The measured cost was 98 ms for 10 monsters at once, so 45-80 monsters means roughly a 0.45-0.8 s host hitch at the moment the night starts.
objections.alternative: Spread spawning over frames, for example a few per frame per district during the first 1-2 s. Or adopt a Lethal-style ramp in which far districts fill in batches over the night. A ramp does not conflict with 'never sleep or despawn by distance'.

objections.target: Population count ('sensible by comparison with Lethal')
objections.problem: Scaling the farm by 5x gives 100-135 monsters on day 1 and 255-340 on day 10, which is not workable on the host. The farm on day 10 (51-68) is already 2-3x Lethal's largest-moon peak for a single facility. Titan allows 18 indoor plus 7 outdoor power, which is about 9-15 indoor and 2-14 outdoor enemies at 1-3 power each, about 12-25 concurrent, reached only late in the day.
objections.alternative: Treat each district (about 200 modules, about a 1-minute spine like one Lethal facility) as one Lethal-moon equivalent and give it a power budget. Suggested CL9 powers: chicken and sheep 1, goose and raccoon 2, pig 3. Per district, day 1 runs from 6 power (near) to 12 power (far), which spans Lethal's Experimentation 4 to Rend 10. Day 10 runs from 12 to 18, which is Titan. At 5x that is about 45 monsters on day 1 (near 5, two mid at 8, two far at 12), about 65 on day 5, and a hard cap of about 80 on day 10. Count is capped by power the way Lethal does it, and the day curve shifts the species mix once the cap is reached. 10x keeps the same per-district budget, about 90 on day 1 and 160 on day 10, and only proceeds if 5x holds its frame budget with 80 monsters all awake.

objections.target: QA plan: 'qa_farm_stage_pie.py and layout tests at the new size'
objections.problem: The script starts timing at cl9.night and samples only at +20, +50 and +90 s. It never measures how long navigation takes after SetSiteMap, or the worst case where the night starts at once. The 500-unit projection extent passes a monster whose own tile is missing as long as a neighbouring tile exists. It also does not force monsters awake, so the 'always active' cost goes untested.
objections.alternative: Add these to the giant QA. Record seconds from SetSiteMap until IsNavigationBeingBuilt is false, along with tile count and navmesh memory. Run a night started immediately after the lobby build. Project with a small extent, about 100 units. Run a pass with every monster forced awake and wandering through a cheat, and record host game-thread ms with stat dumpframe. Add a scripted walk across yards to see client relevancy churn.

objections.target: Replication at district scale (not addressed in the draft)
objections.problem: With the 150 m default cull distance and 390 m districts, players crossing yards make monster actor channels open and close repeatedly on clients. Each re-entry runs LoadData, which sets the skeletal mesh and the ABP. This keeps client CPU bounded, which is good, but the churn cost and any hitch have not been measured.
objections.alternative: Keep the default cull distance and do not make monsters always relevant. Measure re-entry hitches in the yard-walk QA. Only if hitches show up, pool the anim instance or tune NetCullDistance per species.

recommendations: Pathfinding is not the cost problem. Paths are bounded by HomeRange (8-23 m), so per-query A* cost does not depend on map size. About 100 monsters re-pathing every few seconds is negligible. Spend the design effort on navmesh build, ISM gathering and host animation.

Districts must be separate ACL9SiteMap actors, or at least separate ISM component sets, so Recast's per-tile ISM instance scan stays local to a district. State this in the spec and update ACL9SiteMap::Find and SpawnNightPopulation to loop over all districts.
Use fixed district slots in the stage JSON with one NavMeshBoundsVolume per slot from setup_stage.py. Give the yards no navmesh until a yard monster exists. Do not use invokers.
Gate night start on navigation completion on the host (no build in progress), and show 'preparing' in the lobby if needed. The giant QA records time from map build to navigation done.

Keep AI always active, but stop animating unseen monsters on the host: VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption = OnlyTickMontagesWhenNotRendered plus URO on the monster mesh. Check the five ABPs for gameplay-relevant notifies first.

If the host is still over budget after animation culling, add think-rate LOD (for example 5-10 Hz when no player is within about 50 m) with a clamped movement step, citing Lethal's 0.2 s AIIntervalTime as precedent that this still counts as 'always active'.
Time-slice night spawning instead of spawning everything in one frame (98 ms per 10 monsters measured).
